Translate organizational and IT strategy into operating plans, priorities, resource requirements, performance expectations, and measurable outcomes. Advise the CIO and executive leadership on operational performance, information security priorities, portfolio health, vendor exposure, service capacity, and investment priorities. Prepare executive briefings, governance materials, business cases, risk summaries, budget recommendations, and decision requests. Represent Information Technology in enterprise governance forums and act on behalf of the CIO for assigned operational matters. Establish IT service-management standards, operating procedures, service ownership, escalation paths, and performance expectations. Oversee major incident coordination, executive escalation, service restoration, root-cause review, corrective actions, and communications. Ensure operational readiness for implementations, upgrades, major changes, and transitions from project delivery into sustainable support. Establish and monitor service-level expectations, customer satisfaction, first-contact resolution, backlog health, response time, resolution time, and escalation quality. Improve intake, triage, assignment, knowledge management, self-service, automation, communications, and request-fulfillment workflows. Use performance data and customer feedback to drive problem management, training, standardization, automation, and continuous improvement. Information Security Operations Provide leadership and administrative oversight for assigned Information Security Operations personnel and security operations capabilities. Coordinate security monitoring, threat detection, incident response, vulnerability management, identity and access operations, security tooling, regulatory readiness, operational risk management, and performance reporting. Ensure information security risks, audit findings, security incidents, compliance gaps, and remediation commitments have accountable owners, target dates, documented status, and escalation. Provide clear, risk-based reporting to executives and governance bodies regarding security operations performance, threat activity, incident response, vulnerability exposure, regulatory readiness, remediation, and resource needs. Ensure information security requirements are incorporated into projects, procurements, vendor reviews, architecture decisions, operational changes, clinical workflows, and service transitions. IT Project and Portfolio Governance Establish portfolio intake requirements for technology, evaluation, prioritization, sequencing, governance, resource planning, risk management, status reporting, change control, and closure practices. Ensure projects have defined sponsorship, scope, outcomes, timelines, budgets, dependencies, operational owners, readiness criteria, and benefit measures. Review portfolio health and intervene when technology projects face material schedule, budget, scope, resource, vendor, adoption, or operational-readiness risk. Coordinate technology portfolio priorities with the PMO to align with organizational strategy, regulatory commitments, operational capacity, technical roadmaps, information security requirements, and funding. IT Vendor, Contract, and Third-Party Governance Lead governance for strategic, high-risk, and operationally significant technology vendors. Establish accountable ownership, performance standards, service-review cadence, scorecards, escalation processes, and corrective-action expectations. Coordinate technology contract planning, renewals, amendments, statements of work, licensing, support agreements, service levels, and vendor obligations. Monitor vendor cost, utilization, performance, support quality, regulatory posture, contractual compliance, lifecycle risk, concentration risk, and value realization. Maintain forward visibility into renewals, notice periods, price changes, licensing exposure, implementation commitments, and vendor dependencies. Financial, Workforce, and Resource Management Develop and manage assigned operating and capital budgets, forecasts, staffing plans, consulting resources, and contract expenditures. Align staffing, vendor capacity, and project resources with demand, organizational priorities, risk, and operational commitments. Develop workforce plans, succession considerations, role clarity, cross-training, professional-development priorities, and recruitment strategies. Lead, coach, develop, and hold accountable directors, managers, professional staff, consultants, and vendor resources. Governance, Performance, and Continuous Improvement Establish an integrated operating rhythm for service performance, information security operations, project delivery, vendor performance, budget, workforce capacity, and improvement initiatives. Define measurable goals and key performance indicators; use data to guide decisions and hold leaders and partners accountable. Ensure policies, procedures, standards, playbooks, service documentation, knowledge articles, dependency records, and escalation information are current and usable. Promote transparent prioritization, consistent decision-making, operational discipline, documentation, and follow-through. Other Functions Other duties as assigned. Accountable for workforce planning, performance management, coaching, development, succession planning, and appropriate staffing for assigned functions. An equivalent combination of education and progressively responsible experience may be considered in accordance with organizational requirements. Experience Required Ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience in information technology, technology operations, service delivery, information security operations, project or portfolio management, vendor management, or a related field. Demonstrated experience managing budgets, staffing, contracts, vendors, service levels, operational risk, executive reporting, major incidents, and complex initiatives. Preferred Qualifications And Experience Master’s degree in information technology, Information Security, Cybersecurity, Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, or a related field. Leadership experience in a healthcare delivery organization, hospital, tribal health organization, or integrated delivery network. Professional certification such as ITIL, PMP, CISSP, CISM, CGEIT, or a comparable credential. Information security operations, security monitoring, threat detection, incident response, vulnerability management, identity and access operations, regulatory readiness, operational risk, security architecture, and applicable healthcare cybersecurity standards. Project, program, and portfolio governance; financial and resource planning; organizational change; and benefits realization. IT vendor governance, contracting, licensing, performance management, third-party risk, and technology lifecycle management. Skills In Enterprise leadership, strategic planning, operational discipline, prioritization, delegation, coaching, and accountability. Executive communication, facilitation, negotiation, conflict resolution, vendor escalation, and cross-functional influence. Data-informed decision-making, dashboard development, business-case development, and concise executive communication. Ability to Translate strategy into executable plans, measurable outcomes, and clear accountability. Lead multiple functions and concurrent priorities while maintaining attention to patient care, customer experience, risk, quality, and execution.
